faqs.q: In the age of the Buddha, how many mahajanapadas are traditionally recorded?

Consider the following statements regarding Kasi and Kosala:
(I) Kasi's capital was Varanasi, enclosed by mud-walls in the sixth century B.C.
(II) Kasi was initially the most powerful state but eventually submitted to Kosala.
(III) Kosala's city of Ayodhya was settled on a large scale before the sixth century B.C.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Excavations show Ayodhya was not settled on any scale before the sixth century B.C., making statement III incorrect.

(I) It included Sindh, the north-west frontier, and the part of Panjab west of the Indus.

(II) It gave an impetus to Indo-Iranian trade and commerce.
(III) The punch-marked coins found in India were introduced as a direct result of contact with Iran.

faqs.e: It is stated to be wrong to think that punch-marked coins continued in India as a result of contact with Iran.

faqs.e: Bhandagarika refers to the treasurer, not the commander; senanayaka was the term for commander.
